A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a number of proteins that may be involved in the pathogenesis of MTLE HS, and we have identified a subset of proteins whose expression levels are altered in MTLE HS and that are potential biomarkers of MTLE HS.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the proteomic profile of the sclerotic and nonsclerotic epileptogenic hippocampus is distinct, and that the expression levels of proteins that were decreased in the sclerotics were increased in the nonsclerotics.

the proteomic profile of hippocampal tissue in mesial temporal sclerosis is distinct from that of hippocampal tissues without sclerosis, and this profile is likely to be associated with excitotoxic injury.

the expression level of proteins involved in neuronal cell body and dendrite loss is decreased in the sclerotics hippocampi, whereas that of proteins involved in astrocytic hypertrophy and gliosis is increased.
